US-552 AS BUILT, AND THE ONE CALL THAT WANTS ATLAS'S EYE: the script writes to /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt -- the exact file US-524 refused to touch, with a test (test_setGpuCma_neverWritesCmdlineTxt) pinning the refusal. I did NOT treat that refusal as binding forever, and I did not quietly cross it either. Re-derived: US-524's reason was "a safer mechanism exists" (config.txt overlay params; a bad one costs a dark display with SSH alive, a corrupted cmdline.txt costs root= on a Pi that lives in a car). That reason DOES NOT HOLD for an output mode on a Pi 5 -- the legacy config.txt hdmi_group/hdmi_mode/hdmi_cvt path is Pi 4-and-earlier firmware, so the KMS `video=` kernel arg is the only boot-level lever there is. So I paid for the crossing with four interlocks, and THEY ARE AS MUCH THE DELIVERABLE AS THE PIN: (1) the connector is DISCOVERED from /sys/class/drm, never assumed -- a Pi 5 has TWO micro-HDMI ports and pinning the empty one is a silent no-op that still prints "applied"; (2) nothing is written unless EXACTLY ONE connector reads `connected` -- no panel (bench) or two panels means we cannot know, and a guess is a confident wrong answer; (3) the target must be a mode the PANEL ITSELF advertises in EDID; (4) the composed line is verified BEFORE install (one line, root= + every original token present) and re-read after, auto-restoring the pristine backup on disagreement. Both file headers explain the crossing -- without that, the next reader sees only an inconsistency with US-524.

*** INTERLOCK 3 IS ALSO THE STORY'S OPEN UNCERTAINTY AND I LEFT IT AS A REFUSAL DELIBERATELY. If the panel does NOT advertise 480x320 -- a live possibility, and arguably the very REASON the Pi negotiates 1080p -- the script WARNs, prints what the panel does advertise, and pins NOTHING. Forcing a CVT-generated timing the panel never claimed can scan out black, in a car, with no local recovery; that is not a call to make from a Windows box that cannot read the EDID. IF THAT WARN FIRES ON THE NEXT DEPLOY, IT IS AN ATLAS/A-16 EDID FINDING, NOT A BUG IN THE SCRIPT. ***

*** THE GENERALIZABLE PATTERN, AND IT IS WHAT UNBLOCKED THE STORY: when an AC says "read X, and if X is wrong, fix it" and you CANNOT read X -- do not guess, and do not block. IMPLEMENT THE READ AS PART OF THE FIX. The deploy step reads the mode on the Pi every run and decides there. An unknown I could not resolve became a machine-produced finding on the next deploy instead of a human step that never happens. Source is /sys/class/graphics/fb0/virtual_size, NOT the AC's parenthetical kmsprint/xrandr: neither is installed on this Pi (kmsprint needs libdrm-tests; xrandr is X11-only and would read the session, not the scanout). Unreadable -> it prints "unknown" rather than inventing a mode. ***

DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE AC'S CONDITIONAL, FLAGGED FOR PM: the AC says pin "if it is NOT native" and conditionalOutcomes calls an already-native Pi "a no-op verification". I PIN UNCONDITIONALLY (idempotently) and report the observed mode alongside, because an EDID negotiation that happened to land native at THIS boot is not a guarantee for the next one (cable resat, cold panel, OS image update) and the DoD's own words are "deploy SETS the output mode". Where it is already native the pin changes nothing visible -- what it removes is the luck.

EXIT CODES ARE DEPLOY POLICY HERE, WHICH I HAD NOT INTERNALISED BEFORE: deploy-pi.sh runs under `set -e`, so ANY non-zero exit halts the entire deploy. Every deliberate "did not pin" path therefore exits 0 with a loud WARN -- a bench Pi with the panel unplugged is not a deploy failure. Non-zero is reserved for a malformed boot cmdline (1) and a failed write (2), both of which MUST stop the deploy before anyone reboots. Gated by a guard asserting the declared codes are exactly {0,1,2}, so a later edit cannot add a third that turns an unplugged panel into a halted deploy. Note set-gpu-cma.sh's exit 3 does exactly that -- correct for its case, wrong for this one.

My TDD red run reported "18 passed, 32 failed" -- and those 18 were the `file NOT modified` / `no backup written` assertions, all trivially true because the script did not exist yet. Every refusal scenario now ALSO asserts a positive (the exit code + specific WARN content). A safety interlock proven only by "nothing happened" is proven by nothing. ***

SUBTLE TRAP, COST ME A RED: ruleBlock() MUST be line-anchored. A plain `css.index('.takeover-directive {')` finds the STOP OVERRIDE `#dtc-takeover[data-severity="stop"] .takeover-directive {` first, because it is declared EARLIER in the sheet -- so a guard meant to compare an override against its base compares the override against ITSELF and reports 40 > 40 as a passing hierarchy. My first cut had exactly that bug; the pre-existing suite had already solved it (test_dashboard_stop_tier_safety::_ruleBlock, anchored `^`), which is why only MY new test went red. The anchored version now lives in the shared helper.
